narrativeReportMd:
# MedicationAdministration R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking local changes were found. The resource identity is stable, but core fields changed names, cardinality, datatypes, and JSON shape.

## Main migration themes
The largest theme is wire-format rewriting: mandatory `medication[x]` becomes `medication` CodeableReference, mandatory `effective[x]` becomes `occurrence[x]`, reason fields merge, context narrows to encounter, Reference fields become CodeableReference, and category becomes an array. R6→R4 conversion additionally needs policies for Timing, dual-child CodeableReference, Procedure reasons, Group performers, MedicationDispense partOf, CarePlan basedOn, and sub-potency data.

## Scope and exclusions
This report owns local MedicationAdministration changes only. Base Element/DomainResource/Extension noise and search-parameter changes are out of scope.

## Highest-impact findings
Highest impact: medication, occurrence, reason, context/encounter, device/performer CodeableReference, and category singleton-to-array. Human review is needed for EpisodeOfCare, protocol URI, Timing, Group/Procedure/dual CodeableReference, and sub-potency downgrade decisions.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: MedicationAdministration has substantial local breaking changes despite stable artifact identity. The top concerns are mandatory field rewrites (`medication[x]`, `effective[x]`), CodeableReference/merge conversions (`reason`, `device`, `performer.actor`), and R6-only data such as Timing and sub-potency fields.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Use explicit transforms rather than direct validation. Rename/wrap choice and Reference fields, wrap singleton category into an array, classify context references by target type, and define downgrade extensions or rejection policy for R6-only data.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: High for structural deltas because they come directly from primary StructureDefinitions. Medium for rationale and terminology nuance because official diffs, rendered spec pages, live expansions, and ConceptMaps were unavailable.

findings.title: medication[x] changed from a required choice to CodeableReference

oldState.summary: 1..1 CodeableConcept or Reference(Medication), serialized as medicationCodeableConcept or medicationReference.

newState.summary: 1..1 CodeableReference(Medication), serialized as medication with concept/reference children.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by local ElementDefinition path, definition, cardinality, binding, and/or adjacent replacement semantics in the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The element is mandatory, so every R4 instance must rewrite this field before R6 validation. R6 CodeableReference can also carry both concept and reference, which R4 choice syntax cannot represent losslessly.

justification.inferredGoal: Adopt the R6 CodeableReference pattern for code-or-reference medication identity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain R4 `medication[x]` as deprecated while adding a CodeableReference representation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Using `CodeableReference` for medication identity is a coherent R6 modeling goal because it gives one container for coded, referenced, or paired medication identity. A compatibility design exists, but it would leave overlapping same-resource ways to carry a mandatory, safety-relevant field.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could keep the R4 `medication[x]` choice valid, possibly deprecated, and add a new CodeableReference path or choice type for R6 content. That would preserve R4 wire format for code-only and reference-only instances, but systems would need precedence and consistency rules if old and new medication fields were both populated, and the old choice cannot natively preserve an item-level concept/reference pair.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old instances but creates duplicate medication identity paths and still needs rules for paired concept-plus-reference values.

evidence.detail: CodeableReference has concept and reference children.

examples.examplesMd: Map R4 medicationCodeableConcept to medication.concept and medicationReference to medication.reference; dual-child R6 values need review.

findings.narrativeMd: The central medication identity field moved from R4 choice syntax to CodeableReference. This is both a wire-format and generated-model break even though the clinical concept is the same.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 JSON choice properties are unknown in R6. R6 concept-only/reference-only values can map back to R4, but a CodeableReference with both children cannot fit the single R4 choice slot.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Add explicit choice-to-CodeableReference transforms, update serializers/FHIRPath/generated classes, and test code-only, reference-only, and dual-child cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is probably justified for model consistency, but a transition alias would have avoided immediate mandatory field rewrites.

findings.title: effective[x] was renamed to occurrence[x] and Timing was added

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by local ElementDefinition path, definition, cardinality, binding, and/or adjacent replacement semantics in the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The required R4 effective* property is not valid R6 JSON until renamed. R6 occurrenceTiming has no R4 choice equivalent.

justification.inferredGoal: Align event timing with occurrence[x] and allow richer Timing values.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `effective[x]`, update its definition, and add `Timing` as an additional choice type.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goals of clearer occurrence timing and support for `Timing` are reasonable. The hard rename of a required element was not necessary to achieve those functional goals, because R6 could have broadened the existing choice and clarified the wording while leaving old instances valid.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could retain `MedicationAdministration.effective[x]`, add `Timing`, and revise the definition/comment to cover occurrence timing. The tradeoff is living with the older R4 name and relying on documentation, search aliases, or profile guidance for event-pattern consistency.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 data and generated code with the moderate cost of retaining a less event-consistent element name.

evidence.detail: R6 required dateTime, Period, or Timing.

examples.examplesMd: dateTime and Period can be renamed; Timing needs extension, approximation, or downgrade rejection.

findings.narrativeMd: The required administration time field was renamed and widened. Most values are semantically mappable, but every instance and code path must use the new property names.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old effectiveDateTime/effectivePeriod fields fail R6 validation. R6 occurrenceTiming is valid R6 but not representable in R4 without loss or extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename effectiveDateTime→occurrenceDateTime and effectivePeriod→occurrencePeriod. Define policy for occurrenceTiming and update search/FHIRPath logic.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A deprecated alias would have reduced the break but introduced duplicate timing semantics.

findings.title: context became encounter and lost EpisodeOfCare target

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by local ElementDefinition path, definition, cardinality, binding, and/or adjacent replacement semantics in the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 context is an unknown element in R6. Encounter values can be renamed; EpisodeOfCare values violate the R6 target profile.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify that this local context is specifically the encounter.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `context` for R4 Encounter/EpisodeOfCare values while adding or preferring `encounter`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying the element as an encounter-specific link is a reasonable R6 cleanup, and removing EpisodeOfCare reflects a real semantic narrowing. A less-breaking alias design could preserve old instances, but it would keep a broad context field beside the new encounter field and require rules for duplicated Encounter references.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base alternative would keep `context` as a deprecated compatibility element with the old Encounter and EpisodeOfCare targets, while directing new R6 content to `encounter` and perhaps a separate EpisodeOfCare extension or element if that relationship remains important. This preserves R4 data, but it only partially meets the R6 goal because consumers must reconcile `context` and `encounter`, and old broad-context semantics could persist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old references but leaves overlapping encounter/context semantics and weakens the R6 narrowing to Encounter.

examples.examplesMd: Encounter context can be renamed to encounter; EpisodeOfCare needs extension or manual mapping.

findings.narrativeMd: The local encounter/context association was both renamed and narrowed. This is a validation break for any populated R4 context and a data-model gap for EpisodeOfCare.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R6 rejects context. Encounter values can be migrated; EpisodeOfCare values cannot be placed in R6 encounter without violating targetProfile.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Resolve reference types where possible, rename Encounter, and route EpisodeOfCare through an extension or profile-specific convention.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping context or adding episodeOfCare would preserve old data but leave overlapping context semantics.

findings.title: reasonCode and reasonReference merged into reason CodeableReference

oldState.summary: Separate 0..* CodeableConcept reasonCode and 0..* Reference(Condition | Observation | DiagnosticReport) reasonReference.

newState.summary: 0..* CodeableReference targeting Condition, Observation, DiagnosticReport, or Procedure.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by local ElementDefinition path, definition, cardinality, binding, and/or adjacent replacement semantics in the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old reason fields are unknown in R6. R6 Procedure reasons and dual concept/reference CodeableReferences cannot be represented losslessly in R4.

justification.inferredGoal: Consolidate parallel code/reference reason fields and add Procedure reasons.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep deprecated `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` while adding `reason` CodeableReference and the Procedure target.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Unifying coded and referenced reasons under `CodeableReference` and adding Procedure support is a reasonable R6 goal. The less-breaking alias approach would preserve old instances, but it would leave multiple same-resource reason carriers and make item-level concept/reference pairing ambiguous.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base alternative could retain `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` as deprecated aliases for `reason[].concept` and `reason[].reference`. That avoids immediate validation failures, but R6 instances with both concept and reference in one CodeableReference cannot be represented cleanly in the old split arrays without losing the pairing or adding extra reconciliation rules.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 paths but risks duplicate or conflicting reason representations for a clinically important field.

evidence.detail: R4 reasonReference targets Condition, Observation, DiagnosticReport.
R6 reason is CodeableReference and adds Procedure target.

examples.examplesMd: Map reasonCode to reason.concept and reasonReference to reason.reference; Procedure reasons need downgrade policy.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 collapses two R4 arrays into one CodeableReference array. The concept is mappable, but the paths and datatype changed and the target set widened.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 reasonCode/reasonReference fail R6 validation. R6 Procedure or dual-child CodeableReferences cannot cleanly fit R4 reasonReference/reasonCode.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Implement element-by-element transforms and update analytics/search/FHIRPath that refer to old paths.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping deprecated old fields would avoid direct parser failures but require conflict resolution if old and new reason fields coexisted.

findings.title: device and performer.actor changed from Reference to CodeableReference

oldState.summary: device is Reference(Device); performer.actor is Reference(Practitioner | PractitionerRole | Patient | RelatedPerson | Device).

newState.summary: Both elements are CodeableReference; performer.actor also allows Group.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by local ElementDefinition path, definition, cardinality, binding, and/or adjacent replacement semantics in the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Existing Reference objects must be wrapped under CodeableReference.reference. R6 concept-only devices/performers and Group performers have no native R4 representation.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow coded device/performer concepts and group performers when specific instances are unavailable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the Reference elements and add separate coded fields or compatibility aliases for concept-only cases.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing coded device or performer concepts, and Group performers, is a plausible R6 expressiveness goal. Keeping the old Reference shapes would cover common R4 instances and Group could be added as a target, but concept-only and paired concept/reference cases would remain split across fields.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base alternative could retain `device` and `performer.actor` as direct References, add Group to the performer target list, and introduce optional coded siblings for unknown or class-level devices/performers. This is less breaking for old data but materially less clean than a single CodeableReference container and requires conflict rules when a code and reference both appear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 references but splits concept/reference performer and device semantics and cannot fully model paired CodeableReference values.

evidence.detail: R4 performer.actor is Reference with five target profiles.
R6 performer.actor is CodeableReference and adds Group.

examples.examplesMd: R4 references become CodeableReference.reference. R6 concept-only and Group values need extensions or rejection on downgrade.

findings.narrativeMd: These local elements keep their names but not their datatypes. That makes the break easy to miss: object paths survive, while child shape and generated accessor types change.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Strict R6 validators expect CodeableReference items, not bare Reference objects. R6 values using concept or Group cannot be represented in base R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap R4 references, update generated classes, and define downgrade policy for concept-only device/performer and Group performer values.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Separate optional coded fields would have preserved Reference wire compatibility but kept parallel code/reference semantics.

findings.title: category changed from singleton object to repeating array and binding weakened

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R4 local category CodeSystem uses terminology.hl7.org and has inpatient/outpatient/community.

newState.summary: 0..* CodeableConcept with example binding; R6 local CodeSystem adds discharge and uses hl7.org/fhir CodeSystem URL.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R6 binding is example strength; no expansion was run.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by local ElementDefinition path, definition, cardinality, binding, and/or adjacent replacement semantics in the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions.

impact.impactRationaleMd: In FHIR JSON, widening 0..1 to 0..* changes a present category from object to array. R6 multiple categories cannot fit R4 0..1 without policy.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow multiple category classifications and loosen evolving terminology.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `category` as a singleton and add an optional repeating secondary or additional category element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Supporting multiple administration classifications and looser terminology is reasonable. Changing the existing singleton element to repeating creates avoidable JSON and generated-model churn for populated R4 category data, while an additive secondary-category path could meet most of the same goal.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could leave `MedicationAdministration.category` at `0..1` for the primary or legacy category and add a new `additionalCategory` or similarly named repeating element for extra classifications. This preserves R4-valid instances and still allows multiple classifications; the tradeoff is a less elegant split model and the need for validators, search, and display code to union the fields.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 wire shape but adds primary/additional category semantics and requires search/display rules to cover both fields.

evidence.detail: R6 local CodeSystem adds discharge and changes canonical system URL relative to R4 local package.

examples.examplesMd: Wrap singleton R4 category in an array for R6; choose/extend when downgrading multiple R6 categories.

findings.narrativeMd: This is a subtle hard break: increasing cardinality is usually permissive, but FHIR JSON changes a singleton field into an array field.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 category object is not valid R6 JSON for a repeating element. R6 multiple category entries are not representable in R4 0..1 without data loss or extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap category on upgrade. For downgrade, reject multiple categories, select a primary value by policy, or preserve extras in extensions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A separate repeating classification element would preserve old JSON shape but add overlap.

findings.title: instantiates URI was removed; basedOn CarePlan is not equivalent

oldState.summary: 0..* uri for protocol, guideline, orderset, or other definition adhered to.

newState.summary: No instantiates element; new 0..* basedOn Reference(CarePlan).

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by local ElementDefinition path, definition, cardinality, binding, and/or adjacent replacement semantics in the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instantiates is unknown in R6, and URI protocol/order-set links cannot be mechanically converted to CarePlan references. R6 basedOn has no R4 native slot.

justification.inferredGoal: Move from URI definition links to workflow plan fulfillment references.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `instantiates` while adding `basedOn` for CarePlan fulfillment.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of linking administrations to workflow plans is reasonable, but `basedOn` Reference(CarePlan) is not an equivalent replacement for arbitrary protocol, guideline, or orderset URIs. Keeping the optional R4 URI element would preserve existing data without preventing R6 systems from using `basedOn`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could retain `instantiates` as a deprecated URI list and add `basedOn` for actual CarePlan fulfillment. This would avoid forcing protocol links into extensions or lossy mappings; the main cost is continued support for a broad legacy definitional-link field that may overlap with newer workflow relationships.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeps a broad protocol URI link alongside workflow plan references, but the overlap is manageable because the semantics are not equivalent.

evidence.detail: R6 basedOn is 0..* Reference(CarePlan), and instantiates is absent.

examples.examplesMd: Only URI values resolvable to a CarePlan can be mapped natively; otherwise use extension or manual review.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 allowed arbitrary definition/protocol URIs. R6 drops that slot and adds a narrower CarePlan reference. Treat this as removal plus a related new element, not a safe rename.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R6 rejects instantiates. R6 basedOn cannot be represented in base R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Resolve URI semantics; map to CarePlan only when true, otherwise preserve in extension.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping instantiates would have preserved broad URI links but left two planning-related elements.

findings.title: R6 adds recorded and sub-potency fields not native to R4

oldState.summary: No dedicated R4 fields for record-capture time or sub-potency status/reason.

newState.summary: recorded 0..1 dateTime, isSubPotent 0..1 boolean, subPotentReason 0..* CodeableConcept.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by local ElementDefinition path, definition, cardinality, binding, and/or adjacent replacement semantics in the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The additions do not break R4→R6, but dropping sub-potency or record-capture data on downgrade can hide clinically important dose/product-quality information.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent charting time and full-dose/product-quality concerns explicitly.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; optional R6 additions do not break R4-to-R6 validation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The added fields fill plausible clinical and audit gaps, especially around record-capture time and incomplete or compromised administration. Because they are optional additions, the backward-compatible alternative question does not apply to R4-to-R6 base-design breakage.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed to preserve R4 instances. Standard R4 extensions or implementation-guide rules may be useful for downgrade preservation, but those are R6-to-R4 mitigation strategies rather than backward-compatible base R6 alternatives.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: No old-instance break; R6-to-R4 conversion needs extensions or mapping to avoid losing capture-time and sub-potency safety data.

evidence.detail: R6 codes include partialdose, coldchainbreak, recall, adversestorage, expired.

examples.examplesMd: Base R4 needs extensions or lossy notes for these fields.

findings.narrativeMd: These R6-only fields are not forward-breaking but are important for reverse conversion and medication safety.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 validators have no native fields for these values; R6 data using them is valid but not base-R4 representable.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define extensions and do not silently drop computable sub-potency information during downgrade.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Optional additions are backward-compatible for R4→R6; official cross-version extensions would reduce R6→R4 risk.

findings.title: partOf now permits MedicationDispense references

semanticText.comment: MedicationDispense will be used to indicate waste.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by local ElementDefinition path, definition, cardinality, binding, and/or adjacent replacement semantics in the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 data remains valid, but R6 partOf references to MedicationDispense exceed the R4 target profile.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; adding MedicationDispense as a target preserves R4-valid partOf references in R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding MedicationDispense to `partOf` supports the stated waste-link use case and does not invalidate any R4 `partOf` references. Under the calibration rules this is a target-widening and downgrade concern, not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Avoiding the target widening would reduce R6 expressiveness rather than preserve old instance validity. R4-facing profiles, extensions, or conversion rules can handle MedicationDispense links on downgrade, but those are migration mitigations rather than less-breaking base R6 designs.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: No R4-to-R6 break; R6-to-R4 exchange must constrain or map MedicationDispense waste links.

examples.examplesMd: A MedicationDispense target needs an extension or related-resource convention in R4.

findings.narrativeMd: This is a one-way representability risk rather than an R4→R6 break.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Strict R4 target-profile validation cannot accept MedicationDispense in partOf.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Preserve MedicationDispense links via extension or block downgrade when waste lineage matters.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: An extension would be less disruptive but less visible.

findings.title: statusReason broadened from not-performed reason to status-change reason

semanticText.definition: A code indicating why the administration was not performed.

newState.summary: 0..* CodeableConcept: reason status of the administration changed.

semanticText.short: Reason status of the administration changed
semanticText.definition: A code indicating why the status of the administration changed.

facts.oldValue: why the administration was not performed
facts.newValue: why the status of the administration changed

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by local ElementDefinition path, definition, cardinality, binding, and/or adjacent replacement semantics in the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Shape and binding are stable, but R6 producers may use statusReason outside R4 not-performed semantics; R4-era logic may misinterpret it.

justification.inferredGoal: Broaden statusReason to explain more status transitions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `statusReason` limited to not-performed reasons and add a distinct status-change reason element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Explaining broader status transitions is a reasonable goal, but overloading the existing path changes semantics while retaining the old not-given value set. A distinct element would have preserved R4-era interpretation and made broader R6 usage explicit.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could keep `statusReason` for not-performed or negated administrations and add `statusChangeReason` or similar for on-hold, stopped, or other lifecycle-transition explanations. The tradeoff is a slightly larger model and some overlap for not-done cases, but it avoids ambiguous business logic and downgrade interpretation.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds one optional field but avoids silently broadening established business semantics.

evidence.detail: R4 definition is reason administration was not performed.
R6 definition is reason status changed.

examples.examplesMd: Structurally convertible, but semantically broader than R4 not-performed wording.

findings.narrativeMd: The field did not move, so validators will not flag this; the risk is semantic/business logic.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R6-valid statusReason values can be behaviorally different when read by R4-era systems that assume not-given semantics.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit rules around statusReason and constrain or extend broader status-change reasons during downgrade.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A distinct new element would have reduced semantic ambiguity.

findings.title: dosage invariant relaxed to allow text-only dosage

oldState.summary: mad-1 required dose or rate[x] when dosage is present.

constraints.human: SHALL have at least one of dosage.dose or dosage.rate[x]

newState.summary: mad-1 requires text, dose, or rate[x] when dosage is present.

constraints.human: If dosage attribute is present then SHALL have at least one of dosage.text or dosage.dose or dosage.rate[x]

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matched by local ElementDefinition path, definition, cardinality, binding, and/or adjacent replacement semantics in the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 data remains valid, but an R6 dosage with text only is valid in R6 and invalid against R4 mad-1.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; relaxing `mad-1` preserves R4-valid dosage instances in R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Permitting text-only dosage content is a pragmatic R6 relaxation and does not make valid R4 instances invalid. The compatibility issue is that newly valid R6 text-only dosage may not round-trip to R4, which is a down-conversion concern rather than evidence of a less-breaking R6 base design.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base alternative is needed to preserve old instances. Keeping the stricter R4 invariant would reduce R6 expressiveness; R4-facing exchange can use profiles, transformations, or rejection rules for text-only dosage, but those are downgrade strategies.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: No R4-to-R6 break; text-only R6 dosage needs downgrade policy if R4 validation is required.

evidence.detail: R6 permits text as the required dosage content.

examples.examplesMd: Text-only dosage is R6-valid but fails R4 mad-1 if represented directly.

findings.narrativeMd: The local invariant is weaker in R6. This is not a forward break but does matter for R6→R4 conversion.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: New R6 text-only dosage is valid under R6 and invalid under R4 unless transformed or extended.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Detect text-only dosage; derive structured dose/rate only with provenance, otherwise preserve via extension or reject downgrade.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The relaxation is pragmatic; official cross-version extension guidance would reduce risk.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Same canonical URL, id/name, kind resource, type MedicationAdministration, DomainResource base, specialization derivation, and abstract=false.
`status` remains the only local modifier-sensitive element and keeps the same modifier reason.
Existing local summary flags are materially stable; new `recorded` is summary=true and is covered in findings.
No local fixed, pattern, or default values were found.
No local min/max value, maxLength, or regex-style limits were found.
No local slicing changes were identified.
No stronger local invariant was found. The local dosage mad-1 relaxation is reported; inherited ele-1/dom/ext constraints are out of scope.
Required status code literals appear unchanged. Category binding weakening and sub-potency terminology are covered in findings; live expansions were not run.
No local min increases or max decreases were found. Category max widening is still a JSON shape break and is reported.
